description: Identity and attribute statements. The foundation of every Japanese sentence.
example_jp: 私は学生です。
example_en: I am a student.
system_prompt_hint: Generate sentences using です/だ to state identity or attributes. Keep structures simple: [topic]は[noun/adjective]です。

description: Mark the topic of a sentence. Contrasts with が which marks the grammatical subject.
example_jp: 今日は天気がいいです。
example_en: As for today, the weather is nice.
system_prompt_hint: Use は to introduce topics. Practice contrasting topic (は) with subject (が) in the same sentence.

name_en: Existence — います / あります
description: います for animate things (people, animals). あります for inanimate things.
example_jp: 机の上に本があります。猫がいます。
example_en: There is a book on the desk. There is a cat.
system_prompt_hint: Describe scenes using います and あります with location expressions. Use に to mark where things exist.

description: Marks the direct object of a transitive verb.
example_jp: コーヒーを飲みます。
example_en: I drink coffee.
system_prompt_hint: Use を to mark what is being acted upon. Combine with common transitive verbs: 食べる、飲む、見る、書く、読む。

description: The standard polite form for present and future actions.
example_jp: 毎日日本語を勉強します。
example_en: I study Japanese every day.
system_prompt_hint: Use ます/ません for present and future actions. Mix positive and negative forms naturally.

description: Polite past tense. Add time expressions to anchor the action.
example_jp: 昨日、友達に会いました。
example_en: I met a friend yesterday.
system_prompt_hint: Use ました/ませんでした for past events. Include time words: 昨日、先週、去年。

description: Express personal desires. Conjugates like an い-adjective.
example_jp: 日本に行きたいです。
example_en: I want to go to Japan.
system_prompt_hint: Express desires using [verb stem]たい. Try both present desires and past desires (たかった).

description: Express ability. Regular potential: [stem]られる. する→できる, くる→こられる.
example_jp: 日本語が話せます。泳ぐことができます。
example_en: I can speak Japanese. I can swim.
system_prompt_hint: Use potential form to describe abilities and possibilities. Include both できる and the potential conjugation (e.g., 話せる).

name_en: Must / Have to — なければなりません
description: Express obligation. Casual: なきゃ. Alternative: ないといけない.
example_jp: 明日までに宿題を出さなければなりません。
example_en: I have to submit the homework by tomorrow.
system_prompt_hint: Use ～なければなりません for obligations and duties. Contrast with してはいけない (must not).

description: Connect actions in sequence. Essential — used as a base for many other patterns.
example_jp: 朝起きて、シャワーを浴びて、朝ごはんを食べます。
example_en: I wake up, take a shower, and eat breakfast.
system_prompt_hint: Chain actions with て-form to describe a sequence of events, like a morning routine or recipe.

description: Ongoing action OR resulting state. Context determines which meaning applies.
example_jp: 今、本を読んでいます。結婚しています。
example_en: I'm reading now. I am married.
system_prompt_hint: Describe what's happening right now with [verb-te]いる. Also use for states that result from completed actions.

description: Make a polite request. Negative: ないでください (please don't).
example_jp: ここに名前を書いてください。
example_en: Please write your name here.
system_prompt_hint: Write polite instructions, classroom directions, or recipe steps using てください.

description: Action 2 happens strictly after action 1 is complete.
example_jp: 宿題をしてから、テレビを見ます。
example_en: After doing homework, I watch TV.
system_prompt_hint: Use てから to describe ordered activities. Contrast with 前に (before). Focus on daily routines.

description: Completion with nuance: regret, finality, or doing something fully. Casual: ちゃう/じゃう.
example_jp: 全部食べてしまいました。すみません。
example_en: I ate everything. I'm sorry.
system_prompt_hint: Use てしまう for accidental, regrettable, or finalized actions. Try both regretful and neutral completions.

description: Adjectives ending in い. Conjugate directly: negative (-くない), past (-かった).
example_jp: この映画は面白かったです。高くないですね。
example_en: This movie was interesting. It's not expensive, is it.
system_prompt_hint: Describe things using い-adjectives in all 4 forms: present+past × positive+negative.

description: Adjectives that need な before nouns and conjugate with だ/です.
example_jp: 彼女は親切な人です。部屋がきれいじゃなかった。
example_en: She is a kind person. The room wasn't clean.
system_prompt_hint: Use な-adjectives to describe people and things. Practice all forms: な+noun, present/past, positive/negative.

description: AはBより〜 = A is more ~ than B. Bの方がAより〜 = B is more ~ than A.
example_jp: 夏より冬の方が好きです。
example_en: I prefer winter over summer.
system_prompt_hint: Compare two things using より and の方が. Try preferences, qualities, quantities.

description: The most versatile conditional. Natural consequence or hypothesis. Also used for 'when'.
example_jp: 雨が降ったら、家にいます。日本に行ったら、寿司を食べたい。
example_en: If it rains, I'll stay home. When I go to Japan, I want to eat sushi.
system_prompt_hint: Use たら for if/when scenarios. Include both present hypotheticals and future planning.

description: When X happens, Y always follows (natural/automatic). Used for directions, facts, habits.
example_jp: 右に曲がると、コンビニがあります。春になると、桜が咲きます。
example_en: If you turn right, there's a convenience store. When spring comes, cherry blossoms bloom.
system_prompt_hint: Describe natural cause-effect chains: directions, recipes, seasonal events, scientific facts using ～と。

description: If [sufficient condition], then Y. More formal/literary. Often used for advice.
example_jp: 毎日練習すれば、上手になります。
example_en: If you practice every day, you'll get better.
system_prompt_hint: Use ～ば for logical, universal conditions. Works well for advice and general truths.

description: Based on what you said / assuming that. Used when the condition is hypothetical or based on new information.
example_jp: 日本に行くなら、京都に寄ってみてください。
example_en: If you're going to Japan, stop by Kyoto.
system_prompt_hint: Use なら for advice based on a situation the listener has mentioned. Practice with travel, recommendations.

description: Explains reason after stating the consequence. Plain or polite before から.
example_jp: 疲れているから、早く寝ます。
example_en: Because I'm tired, I'll sleep early.
system_prompt_hint: Connect consequences to their reasons using から. Try reversing order: cause + から + effect.

description: More polite/formal reason. Implies the result naturally follows. Softer than から.
example_jp: 雨が降っているので、傘を持ってきました。
example_en: Since it's raining, I brought an umbrella.
system_prompt_hint: Use ので for formal writing, apologies, and polite explanations. Contrast tone with から.

description: Expresses disappointment or surprise: 'even though X, unexpectedly Y'.
example_jp: あんなに勉強したのに、試験に落ちてしまった。
example_en: Even though I studied so much, I failed the exam.
system_prompt_hint: Use のに to express frustration, surprise, or disappointment. The result contradicts expectations.

name_en: Giving — あげる / くれる
description: あげる: I/we give to others. くれる: others give to me/my group. Direction relative to speaker is key.
example_jp: 友達にプレゼントをあげた。先生が本をくれた。
example_en: I gave my friend a present. The teacher gave me a book.
system_prompt_hint: Practice あげる and くれる with different social relationships: friends, family, teachers. Direction matters.

description: Receive something from someone. Focus is on the receiver. Source marked with に or から.
example_jp: 誕生日に友達からケーキをもらいました。
example_en: I received a cake from my friend for my birthday.
system_prompt_hint: Describe receiving things or favors. Use both に and から for the giver.

name_en: Doing Favors — てあげる / てもらう / てくれる
name_jp: 〜てあげる・てもらう・てくれる
description: Extend giving/receiving to actions, not just objects.
example_jp: 弟に宿題を教えてあげた。友達に送ってもらった。
example_en: I taught my brother his homework. I had my friend drive me.
system_prompt_hint: Describe acts of kindness between people. Focus on who benefits from the action.

description: The action is received by the subject. Often implies being affected (negatively).
example_jp: 先生に褒められた。電車で足を踏まれた。
example_en: I was praised by the teacher. I had my foot stepped on in the train.
system_prompt_hint: Describe events where things happen TO the subject. Include both neutral and nuisance passives.

description: Make or let someone do something. Context determines 'make' vs 'allow'.
example_jp: 親は子どもに部屋を掃除させる。好きな音楽を聴かせてあげた。
example_en: Parents make children clean the room. I let them listen to their favorite music.
system_prompt_hint: Describe authority relationships (parent/child, boss/employee) or acts of permission using させる.

description: Forced against one's will. Heavy nuance of unwilling obligation. Casual: させられる→さされる.
example_jp: 上司に残業させられた。子供の頃、野菜を食べさせられた。
example_en: I was made to work overtime by my boss. As a child, I was made to eat vegetables.
system_prompt_hint: Express reluctant compliance or unwilling obligation. Use with complaints and past hardships.

description: Expresses possibility or uncertainty (50% or less). More doubtful than だろう.
example_jp: 明日は雨が降るかもしれません。
example_en: It might rain tomorrow.
system_prompt_hint: Express uncertainty about weather, future events, or speculation. Contrast with でしょう (more certain).

description: Express opinions and assumptions. Use plain form before と思う.
example_jp: この問題は難しいと思います。彼は来ないと思う。
example_en: I think this problem is difficult. I don't think he's coming.
system_prompt_hint: Share opinions and predictions using と思う. Practice with current events, preferences, future plans.

name_en: Hearsay — そうだ / らしい
description: そうだ: direct information from a source. らしい: inferred from indirect evidence.
example_jp: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れるそうです。彼は風邪らしい。
example_en: According to the forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow. He seems to have a cold.
system_prompt_hint: Report what you've heard or infer from indirect evidence. Contrast the certainty levels of そうだ and らしい.

name_en: Appearance — ようだ / みたいだ
description: Describe appearance or make inferences from direct evidence. みたいだ is more casual.
example_jp: 彼女は悲しいようです。まるで夢みたいだ。
example_en: She seems to be sad. It's like a dream.
system_prompt_hint: Describe how things appear from visible evidence. Use both ようだ (formal) and みたいだ (casual).

description: Turn a verb phrase into a noun. こと: conceptual/formal. の: experiential/perceptual.
example_jp: 泳ぐことが好きです。彼が来るのを見た。
example_en: I like swimming. I saw him come.
system_prompt_hint: Use こと to talk about activities in general, and の to describe direct experiences or perceptions.

description: Modify nouns with verb or adjective clauses placed before the noun. No relative pronoun needed.
example_jp: 昨日読んだ本は面白かったです。
example_en: The book I read yesterday was interesting.
system_prompt_hint: Describe things using relative clauses. Start with simple patterns: [verb]＋noun, [adj]＋noun.

name_en: In order to — ために / ように
description: ために: purposeful goal with volitional verbs. ように: desired result, often for potential/neg verbs.
example_jp: 健康のために運動します。忘れないようにメモする。
example_en: I exercise for my health. I take notes so I don't forget.
system_prompt_hint: Describe goals and intentions. ために for conscious goals, ように for hoped-for states or abilities.

description: Even if / even though. The result holds regardless of the condition.
example_jp: どんなに疲れていても、諦めません。
example_en: No matter how tired I am, I won't give up.
system_prompt_hint: Express resilience, conditions that don't affect outcomes. Combine with どんなに for emphasis.

name_en: Without doing — ずに / ないで
description: ずに is more formal/literary. ないで is everyday speech. Describe what is not done.
example_jp: 何も言わずに部屋を出た。朝ごはんを食べないで来た。
example_en: I left the room without saying anything. I came without eating breakfast.
system_prompt_hint: Describe skipped actions or missing steps. Use ずに in formal writing, ないで in dialogue.

name_en: Polite Requests — ていただけませんか
description: Very polite request form. Hierarchy: てください < てもらえますか < ていただけませんか.
example_jp: もう一度説明していただけませんか。
example_en: Could you please explain again?
system_prompt_hint: Write polite requests for formal situations: office, customer service, strangers. Compare with casual forms.

description: Lower yourself to raise the other person. Used in business/formal contexts.
example_jp: 荷物をお持ちします。後でご連絡いたします。
example_en: I will carry your luggage. I will contact you later.
system_prompt_hint: Practice humble expressions for service situations: reception, customer service, formal emails.
